q1_issues.issue: 'shot an 8-under 64' is encoded as a Measure whose scale (score) and unit (stroke) appear nowhere in the text, and the direct-object NP itself receives no witness or role atom on the shoot event.
This MoreBy introduces 'par', an untyped comparison standard the sentence never mentions, and uses 'few' as the scale although the comparative rules require the surface adjective.

'with a one-stroke lead over Kenny Perry' is re-expressed as a MoreBy comparative on an invented 'few' scale, dropping the 'lead' NP, severing the PP from the entering event, and inverting the direction by golf world knowledge.

q2_gaps: a bare-numeral NP naming a sports score with a relative-to-par modifier ('shot an 8-under 64') — no stated scale or unit for Measure, and no licensed carrier for 'N-under'
a noun-headed measured advantage PP ('with a one-stroke lead over X')
a fronted free participial adjunct ('Buoyed by advice ..., Howell shot ...') — whether and how it attaches to the matrix clause
notes: The reduced relative 'advice imparted by Nicklaus', the by-phrase mapped to Agent, the purpose infinitive (To shoot enter) with a tenseless complement, and the bare deictic 'today' all follow the instruction set. Every defect sits in the two numeric golf expressions.
